verdict: Kimberly-Clark's sales were flat at $4.1B and operating profit fell 17%, but a $1.4B gain on its IFP joint-venture deal pushed total net income to $1.8B.

kpis.label: IFP deal gain
kpis.note: pre-tax gain on completing the IFP transaction

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Huggies, Kleenex, Cottonelle and other brands in North America — sales up 0.9%, with 2.0% volume growth partly offset by more promotions.

segments.name: International Personal Care
segments.note: Personal care outside North America — sales down 2.8%, as a China social-media disruption cut organic sales by about 770 basis points in this segment.

opex.name: Marketing, research & general
opex.note: Marketing brands like Huggies and Kleenex, research, and general running costs.

opex.name: Other expense, net
opex.note: Other operating expense, net, inside operating profit.

otherDetail: Below operating profit: net interest and nonoperating expense took $45M, tax took $95M, and then two large items lifted the total — $29M of income from equity companies and $1,395M of income from discontinued operations (mainly the ~$1.4B pre-tax gain on completing the IFP transaction), less $7M attributable to noncontrolling interests. Net income attributable to Kimberly-Clark was $1,793M.
oneTimers: Income from discontinued operations was $1,395M, including a pre-tax gain of about $1.4B on completing the IFP Transaction (the Arbex joint venture with Suzano) on July 1, 2026, and $52M of pre-tax separation costs.

Operating profit included $106M of Kenvue acquisition costs and $55M of 2024 Transformation Initiative charges; excluding these and other items, adjusted operating profit was $677M. Kimberly-Clark closed its Kenvue acquisition on November 2, 2026, after quarter-end.
footerNote: Headline results in the release are for continuing operations (the IFP business is now in discontinued operations). This page's bottom line is total net income attributable to Kimberly-Clark ($1,793M, $5.37 per diluted share), so the discontinued-operations gain is shown below the operating line and explained in Other income — continuing-operations EPS was $1.19.

takeaways.title: Organic sales slipped
takeaways.text: Net sales were $4,134M, down 0.4%. Organic sales fell 1.3%, including a roughly 270-basis-point hit from a China social-media disruption and retailer inventory swings in North America.

takeaways.title: Operating profit fell on one-off costs
takeaways.text: Operating profit fell 17% to $516M, including $106M of Kenvue deal costs and $55M of transformation charges. Excluding items, adjusted operating profit was $677M, down 0.9%.

takeaways.title: A deal gain swamped the quarter
takeaways.text: Completing the IFP joint-venture transaction produced a gain of about $1.4B inside discontinued operations, taking total net income to $1,800M and total EPS to $5.37 — most of it one-time.

follow100Note: The $100 view is unusual this quarter: a $33.80-per-$100 gain from discontinued operations (the IFP deal) sits below the operating line, which is why profit kept ($43.37) is far above what the ongoing business earned ($1.19 continuing EPS).
